items.author: main session (military kit rulings, 2026-10-27)
items.title: Fold the military kit into the Digitisation tree: about forty kit items as nodes
items.design: Ben, 2026-10-27: kit is researched in the age tree, not a ladder of its own (RESEARCH.md § What technology is for; MILITARY.md § Land — the classes). research/MILITARY_KIT.md § 2 lists the items (two slots a class, gens 1-3). DESIGN PASS FIRST: the tree's grammar holds about fifteen nodes a branch (RESEARCH.md § The shape of an age's tree), so place the kit by subject across branches — small arms, section weapons, guns and protection in Force; armour materials in Processing; sensors, fire control, drones and networked kit in Signal & Orbit — as minors and majors in clusters, keeping each major's two-minors rule; say where the grammar must widen and put that to Ben. Then the store edit (tech_tree_store.js --check, gen_tech_tree_table.js), each node naming its kit as an unlock effect (unread until BL-1434, unit designs). Ben, 2026-11-03: air units' kit moves onto the new kit goods too; FPV drones sit inside the drones good, not a good of their own. RULED (Ben, 2026-11-03, kit tree form, on the design pass in research/MILITARY_KIT.md § 8): (1) one node per technology, opening that technology's item in every class it fits - 39 kit nodes, 33 new and 6 existing nodes gaining a kit unlock; the catalogue's 'two items share a research node' check is relaxed. (2) Accept the wider kit branches (Force 32, Signal & Orbit 29, Processing 23). (3) NO kit spur: kit clusters lengthen the existing arms. (4) Minors may open kit; surge items sit on majors. (5) No cross-branch requirements; the tie is electronics drawn off the shelf. (6) A sixth kit good, airframes (resource_count and save format change). (7) The kit link lives in both places: the store's unlock_kit effect for display, the catalogue's research-node link the read path, tech_tree_store.js --check cross-checks them. (8) The age runs slower: the +27% research cost is not re-tuned away.

items.author: main session (Ben, 2026-10-27)
items.title: After construction capacity: processors finish faster than their inputs; G1 at tick 50 under its gate
items.design: Ben, 2026-10-27: merge BL-1438 (retire construction capacity), keep G1t50 at 85, and treat the new starvation and decommissions as follow-on work. market_viability FULL on main at 9503aa06: G1 92.9, G1t50 78.9 (FAIL; 2106/2668), G1b 3.1, G2 186.3, G3 100.0. In the lane's 16-seed tick-50 totals, processors built 1446 -> 2762, running 1269 -> 2195, input-starved 32 -> 158, decommissioned 54 -> 209. Measure first: which recipes starve, which inputs are short, and whether the scorer now over-builds processors ahead of their extractors (no capacity throttle remains). Fix the cause in the world (input supply, build sequencing by the scorer); never lower the gate or clamp builds to pass it. CARRIED to sprint 59 (Ben, 2026-10-28: cut with G1t50 failing). Main at 302bba15: market_viability FULL G1 93.3 G1t50 79.8 (FAIL) G1b 2.8 G2 191.0 G3 100.0 after the own-market ceiling rule. The remaining gap: power plants over-built into glutted grids (the held bl1232 scorer gate), state buildings left unfunded, remote spare the trade pass does not move, household goods priced over the ceiling; construction draws push steel over the ceiling where steel-using plants stand. MEASURED (main 2f697f80, 2026-11-03, market_viability full --dump-t50): G1t50 82.6 (1830/2215); 53 more running plants clear 85. The 385 not running: input-starved 156 (refined copper <- copper ore 27, atmospheric propellant <- refined fuel 25, consumer goods <- food rations 24, silicon <- silica 11, hydroponics <- water 9, food rations <- agricultural produce 9); decommissioned 124 (65 after starving - consumer goods 17, propellant 8, electronics 8, machinery 7; 43 while RUNNING - oil power plant 17, hydroponics 8, coal power plant 7: the loss reflex idling plants that produce, i.e. glutted power and water); other 61, of which 19 STEEL plants never filed a report row since the build (a lead: a steel recipe or placement the report never covers); no labour 44 (steel 14, refined fuel 8). Not a construction artefact: 139 sites still building at tick 50 are outside the denominator already. Leads in order: (1) why 19+6 steel plants file no row; (2) the intermediate chains copper ore, refined fuel and food rations under-supplied to their consumers - the scorer building consumers ahead of the feeder; (3) power plants over-built into glutted grids, killed by the loss reflex (the held bl1232 scorer gate). RULED (Ben, 2026-11-04, starvation form): the G1t50 gate is re-ruled to 84 (trajectory noise about +/-1 point); the run reserve and the pending-supply forecast land as corrected estimates; the power grid gate goes to BL-1485 (power grid measure); the glut veto ratio stays 2.0; the broke-nation spiral is BL-1482.

items.author: main session (cold review of BL-1434/BL-1446)
items.title: Hire and refit check goods by price as well as quantity; the PNG inflate gets an output cap
items.design: Cold review of unit designs, 2026-10-28. (1) HIGH, latent until later kit unlocks (BL-1436): hire_goods_affordable counts shelf quantity only, while buy_from_corp_shelves charges the posted price capped by purse_room_of, and debit_kit_goods ignores how much it bought. A design refit (0 credits) with a committed treasury gets its kit free; a hire at exact room drops the treasury below its commitments. The row-goods leg had the flaw already. Fix: the affordability check sums qty x posted price plus the credit cost against purse_room_of, and apply asserts the bought amount. (2) LOW: hire_goods_affordable prices each row axis at its first candidate without the kit draw on the same resource, so an affordable hire can be refused. (3) LOW: png_decode.cpp inflate has no output cap; stop once out exceeds h x (stride+1). (4) LOW: the refit menu labels a design refit with the row gate (+ kit) and omits the changed slots goods; an obsolete own row moves the (live design) entry to the end.

items.author: main session (sprint 61, Lane S hand-back, 2026-11-03)
items.title: A nation whose treasury reaches 0 never recovers
items.design: Found by BL-1442 (post-capacity starvation), 2026-11-03: mostly minors build a steel plant in play ticks 1-10, the treasury reaches 0, the funding gate idles every building, income is 0 for good. Nothing runs so nothing earns. About 25 of the plants behind G1t50's gap. The fix is a design question first (FINANCE.md owns it): a floor that keeps the cheapest earners running, debt, or a solvency reserve in the scorer (measured -0.6 pp G1t50 alone, patch scratchpad bl1442_scorer_measured_not_landed.patch). Check: market_viability full tier, count of nations at treasury 0 for 20+ ticks. RULED (Ben, 2026-11-04): a scorer solvency reserve - the scorer does not commit a build that would leave its own nation unable to stay solvent. Built in the same lane as BL-1485 (power grid measure). MEASURED 2026-11-04 (Lane W): a scorer solvency reserve (one more tick of the nation's whole book on top of capex and the run reserve) failed G1t50 (81.9 vs 84) and left nations broke 20+ ticks at 97 of 593 by t50; parked on branch bl1482-solvency-reserve-gate-fail (aab74893). RULED (Ben, 2026-11-04): measure first - split broke-at-handoff from build-then-zero across the 16 seeds, then bring the design back. MEASURED 2026-11-04 (Lane W, BR line): of 98 nations broke 20+ ticks by t50 (593 nations, 16 seeds), 20 were broke from the handoff, 4 built and then went broke (no steel plant among them), 74 were solvent at the handoff and went broke with no build of their own in the 10 ticks before - a structural income shortfall, not a build spiral. RULED (Ben, 2026-11-04): earners keep running - at a treasury of 0 the funding gate still runs a nation's cheapest net-positive buildings, so income restarts (FINANCE.md). The scorer reserve is dropped.

items.title: The loss reflex's recipe rescue retools to power only on a grid that is short
items.design: Found by BL-1485 (power grid measure), 2026-11-04: 59 of 60 play-built power plants by t50 are not builds but the loss reflex's cross-group recipe rescue (economy_system.cpp, 'Recipe rescue'): a floored steel plant retools to power because power's price/base beats a floored output, on grids the measure reads as not short (55 of 59; mean power price 0.75 of base; seed 37: draw 143.7 vs output 738, six steel plants switch in one tick). RULED (Ben, 2026-11-04): gate the rescue now on the same grid measure (body_power_grid_gap, own buildings live, others nominal), for every nation including the player's - the rescue is a mechanical reflex, not a strategic act. A rescue onto power is refused unless the target grid is short. Check: market_viability full tier (G1t50 >= 84, power plants decommissioned at t50 and the PW line against the BL-1485 reading), world_determinism, building_upkeep. MEASURED 2026-11-04 (Lane W): the gate cut play-built power plants 71 -> 15 (none decommissioned) but G1t50 fell to 83.6 (floor 84): the steel plants it no longer rescues stay idle. Parked on branch bl1492-rescue-grid-gate-g1t50-fail (7316da4e). RULED (Ben, 2026-11-04): rescue elsewhere - a refused power rescue tries the next-best non-power recipe before idling; then re-gate. The loss reflex keeps skipping the player's nation (Ben, 2026-11-04: keep the skip), so the gate binds rivals only.

items.title: grudge_sentiment_harness G7f fails: the history is not unchanged with grudge weights zeroed
items.design: Found 2026-11-04 verifying BL-1470 (sentiment contributors): G7f ('the history is UNCHANGED - the sim's scorer reads no grudge', BL-827) fails identically on 41ad4e7c and 286bd8b6, so it predates BL-1470. Lane Y's unconfirmed guess: the check zeroes four grudge weights but not the treaty-broken and faith-sundered ones. Diagnose which is wrong - the check or a scorer that now reads a grudge - before changing anything; never weaken it to pass.
